The open-branch discriminating probe is the targeted low-cost measurement needed before choosing among the plausible siphon and sink-coupled alternatives.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit node Q or R directly
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Both candidate laws require sink-gradient variation, and the archive explicitly calls for an open-branch probe when the pilot span is below 0.08.
Trajectory data targets memory ODE models, while the observed pilot signatures indicate a static monotone-concave response; no evidence requires that cost.
It is explicitly irrelevant to resolving the current model ambiguity.
